theme.title: Emmanuel: God With Us
theme.summary: From the manger to the Jordan: each day keeps what the Church keeps that day, from the Word made flesh to the Father naming his beloved Son.

topics.name: Christmas
topics.summary: The season as a whole: the infancy Gospels, the Incarnation, the Mother of God, the Epiphany, the Baptism of the Lord and the saints of the season.

levels.title: The Baptism of the Lord and Ours

topics.name: Christmas Challenge
topics.summary: One day of the season at a time, from the Nativity to the Baptism of the Lord.

levels.title: The Word Became Flesh
levels.reflection: Tonight the promise has a name. The eternal Son of the Father, through whom all things were made, is born of the Virgin Mary in a stable at Bethlehem. Heaven's glory shows itself in poverty: a manger, swaddling clothes, a few shepherds keeping watch. The Church never tires of singing of this night, because here God does not send a message about salvation; he comes himself, to save us, to show us his love, to be our model of holiness and to make us sharers in his own life. Stay at the manger a while today. Everything the prophets waited for is lying in the straw.

scripture.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

saint.name: St. Romanos the Melodist
saint.reference: Kontakion of the Nativity, as quoted in CCC 525
saint.text: The Virgin today brings into the world the Eternal and the earth offers a cave to the Inaccessible. The angels and shepherds praise him and the magi advance with the star, For you are born for us, Little Child, God eternal!

levels.title: The First to Follow
levels.reflection: The day after Christmas the Church wears red. St. Stephen, one of the seven men chosen by the community in Jerusalem, was full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and he did great wonders among the people. When he was stoned for bearing witness to Christ, he prayed as his Lord had prayed on the cross: that his killers be forgiven, and that the Lord receive his spirit. The Child of Bethlehem was born to give his life, and the first of his followers to die for him shows us what that life looks like in a human heart. Among those watching was a young man named Saul.

scripture.text: And they stoned Stephen, invoking, and saying: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

saint.name: St. Ignatius of Antioch
saint.reference: Letter to the Romans 6, 1-2, as quoted in CCC 2474
saint.text: It is better for me to die [in order to unite myself] to Christ Jesus than to reign over the ends of the earth. I seek him who died for us; I desire him who rose for us.

levels.title: The Home at Nazareth
levels.reflection: On the Sunday after Christmas the Church keeps the feast of the Holy Family. For most of his life Jesus lived as most people live: ordinary days, manual work, prayer with his family and his town, obedient to Mary and Joseph. That hidden obedience was already beginning to undo what Adam's disobedience had destroyed. Nazareth teaches without speeches: a lesson of silence, a lesson on family life, a lesson of work. Your own home can be a domestic church, a place where faith, hope and charity are learned at the kitchen table. Pray for your family today, and do one ordinary thing for them with great love.

scripture.text: And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart.

saint.name: Pope St. Paul VI
saint.reference: Address at Nazareth, 5 January 1964, as quoted in CCC 533
saint.text: The home of Nazareth is the school where we begin to understand the life of Jesus - the school of the Gospel.

levels.title: Darkness Against the Light
levels.reflection: The joy of Christmas is not naive. When the wise men did not return to him, Herod had the boys of Bethlehem killed, two years old and under. The Church honors these Holy Innocents as martyrs: they died in place of the Child, before they could speak his name. The Catechism says the flight into Egypt and this massacre show the opposition of darkness to the light, and that Christ's whole life was lived under the sign of persecution. Yet the darkness did not win. Joseph rose in the night and took the Child and his mother to safety. Pray today for every child whose life is threatened.

scripture.text: Then Herod perceiving that he was deluded by the wise men, was exceeding angry; and sending killed all the men children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the borders thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently inquired of the wise men.

levels.title: A Light for the Gentiles
levels.reflection: When the days of purification were over, Mary and Joseph carried Jesus to the Temple to present him to the Lord. Simeon, a just and devout old man, had been told by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before seeing the Christ. He took the Child in his arms and blessed God: now he could go in peace, because his eyes had seen salvation, a light for the Gentiles and the glory of Israel. Then he told Mary that a sword would pierce her soul. Tonight, before you sleep, pray his words too: you have seen the Light.

scripture.text: A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.

levels.title: Anna, Who Never Left the Temple
levels.reflection: Anna is easy to miss in the Gospel: a few lines about an old widow. But St. Luke takes care to tell us her father's name, her tribe and her age. For decades she had stayed in the Temple, fasting and praying night and day. She had waited most of her life, and when the Child was carried in, she knew him. She gave thanks to God and spoke about him to everyone who was looking for the redemption of Israel. Faithful prayer, kept up through long and quiet years, gave her eyes to see. The Lord does not forget anyone who waits for him.

scripture.text: Now she, at the same hour, coming in, confessed to the Lord; and spoke of him to all that looked for the redemption of Israel.

levels.title: In the Beginning Was the Word
levels.reflection: On the last day of the year the Gospel goes back before time began. St. John does not start with Bethlehem; he starts with eternity: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things were made through him. The Child in the manger is that Word, the light that shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it. To everyone who receives him he gives power to become children of God. As you look back over this year, thank him for every grace, ask pardon for every failure, and give him the year to come.

scripture.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

saint.name: St. Athanasius
saint.reference: On the Incarnation 54, 3, as quoted in CCC 460
saint.text: For the Son of God became man so that we might become God.

levels.title: Theotokos
levels.reflection: The year begins with Mary. On the eighth day of Christmas the Church honors her with her greatest title: Mother of God. The One she conceived by the Holy Spirit and bore at Bethlehem is not merely a holy man; he is the eternal Son of the Father, made man. That is why the Council of Ephesus in 431 confessed her Theotokos, the God-bearer. On this day, too, the Child was circumcised and given the name the angel had announced: Jesus. In most of the United States today is a holy day of obligation. Begin the year at Mass, in the care of the Mother who kept all these things in her heart.

scripture.text: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law:

saint.name: The Liturgy of the Hours
saint.reference: 1 January, Antiphon I of Evening Prayer, as quoted in CCC 526
saint.text: O marvellous exchange! Man's Creator has become man, born of the Virgin. We have been made sharers in the divinity of Christ who humbled himself to share our humanity.

levels.title: Two Friends Who Defended the Faith
levels.reflection: Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen were both from Cappadocia, in what is now Turkey, and became friends as students. Gregory later wrote that it seemed as if they had one soul in two bodies. Both became bishops, and both spent their strength defending the faith of Nicaea in one God in three Persons, when many around them had abandoned it. Basil founded communities of prayer and cared for the poor; Gregory preached so well on the Trinity that he was called "the Theologian". Their friendship was not an escape from holiness but a road to it. Thank God today for the friends who help you believe.

scripture.text: He said: I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaias.

saint.name: St. Gregory Nazianzen
saint.text: Let us be buried with Christ by Baptism to rise with him; let us go down with him to be raised with him; and let us rise with him to be glorified with him.

levels.title: The Nations Come to the Light
levels.reflection: In the United States the Epiphany is celebrated today, on the Sunday between January 2 and January 8. Wise men from the East saw a star and set out to find the newborn King. They asked at Jerusalem, learned from the Scriptures that he would be born in Bethlehem, and when the star stood over the house, they rejoiced with great joy. They fell down, adored him, and opened their treasures: gold, frankincense and myrrh. In them the Gospel sees the first of all the nations coming to Christ. Every one of us who was not born into Israel is in that procession. Bring him your own treasure today.

scripture.text: And entering into the house, they found the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they adored him; and opening their treasures, they offered him gifts; gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

levels.title: A Daughter of the United States
levels.reflection: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton was born and raised in New York in the Episcopal Church. She was a wife and mother, and was widowed young. Through great suffering, and the friendship of a Catholic family in Italy, she came into the Catholic Church, at a high cost. She went on to found at Emmitsburg, in the Archdiocese of Baltimore, the Sisters of Charity of Saint Joseph's, the first congregation of religious women founded in the United States, devoted to the poor and to parish schools. When Pope Paul VI canonized her in 1975 he called her the first daughter of the United States to be declared a saint. Holiness is for every state of life.

scripture.text: Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect.

saint.name: Second Vatican Council
saint.reference: Lumen gentium 40, as quoted in CCC 2013
saint.text: All Christians in any state or walk of life are called to the fullness of Christian life and to the perfection of charity.

levels.title: A Bishop for the Immigrants
levels.reflection: St. John Neumann was born in Bohemia in 1811. When his ordination was delayed at home, he crossed the ocean, poor and alone, to New York, and was ordained there. He became a Redemptorist and later Bishop of Philadelphia. He worked tirelessly for children's instruction in the faith and for Catholic schools, spent himself hearing confessions and visiting his people, and spread the Forty Hours Devotion to the Blessed Sacrament through his parishes. Pope Paul VI called him the honor of all immigrants. Like Jesus looking at the crowd, he saw sheep without a shepherd and gave his life to care for them. Pray today for every immigrant family.

scripture.text: And Jesus going out saw a great multitude: and he had compassion on them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.

levels.title: The Doorkeeper
levels.reflection: Today the Church in the United States may keep the memory of St. André Bessette. Born in Quebec, he knew suffering and poverty from childhood, and with very little schooling he joined the Congregation of Holy Cross and was given the humblest job: porter at a college in Montreal. For years he opened the door to everyone who came, listened to their troubles and prayed with them. He had an oratory to St. Joseph built on Mount Royal, and he cared for it until his death in 1937. Little things done with great faith can open the door of heaven for others. Who comes to your door today?

scripture.text: For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he spoke with them, and said to them: Have a good heart, it is I, fear ye not.

levels.title: Today This Scripture Is Fulfilled
levels.reflection: Jesus came back to Nazareth, where he had grown up, and on the sabbath he went to the synagogue as he always did. He was handed the book of the prophet Isaiah and read: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. Then he sat down and said that today this Scripture was fulfilled. The name Christ means exactly this: the Anointed One, priest, prophet and king. The Child of Bethlehem has grown up, and his mission has begun. By Baptism and Confirmation you share in his anointing. Where is he sending you today?

scripture.text: And he began to say to them: This day is fulfilled this scripture in your ears.

levels.title: Lord, If You Wish
levels.reflection: A man full of leprosy saw Jesus and fell on his face. He did not doubt that Jesus could heal him; he only asked whether he would: Lord, if you will, you can make me clean. Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, the one whom no one would touch, and said: I will. Be cleansed. The Catechism says Christ came to heal the whole man, soul and body, and that his compassion for the sick goes so far that he identifies himself with them. Bring him today whatever in you needs healing, and trust his answer. Then visit, call or pray for someone who is sick.

scripture.text: And stretching forth his hand, he touched him, saying: I will. Be thou cleansed. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.

levels.title: He Must Increase
levels.reflection: John the Baptist had disciples and crowds of his own. When they told him that people were now going to Jesus instead, he was not jealous. He called himself the friend of the bridegroom, who rejoices to hear the bridegroom's voice, and said: He must increase, but I must decrease. The Catechism calls John the last of the prophets and the Lord's immediate forerunner, who pointed him out as the Lamb of God. The whole of Christian life is in John's sentence. Look today for one small way to let Christ increase in you: a moment of prayer instead of noise, a kindness instead of a complaint.

scripture.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

levels.title: This Is My Beloved Son
levels.reflection: Christmas ends at the river Jordan. Jesus, now a grown man, comes from Nazareth and asks John to baptize him. He has no sin to wash away, yet he steps into the water with sinners, already taking our place. The heavens open, the Spirit comes down like a dove, and the Father's voice says: Thou art my beloved Son. In your own Baptism the same Father spoke to you, the same Spirit came upon you, and you became a child of God. Find out the date of your Baptism, and thank God for it today. Tomorrow the Church returns to Ordinary Time, carrying Christmas with her.

scripture.text: And there came a voice from heaven: Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

saint.name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
saint.reference: Commentary on Matthew 2, 5, as quoted in CCC 537
saint.text: Everything that happened to Christ lets us know that, after the bath of water, the Holy Spirit swoops down upon us from high heaven and that, adopted by the Father's voice, we become sons of God.

questions.prompt: In John 1:14, what does St. John say the Word did?
choices: Wrote the Law on tablets of stone
Appeared to the prophets in a dream
Came down as an angel to the shepherds
Was made flesh, and dwelt among us
questions.correctAnswer: Was made flesh, and dwelt among us
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us." The Church calls this the Incarnation.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, who were the first witnesses of Jesus' birth?
choices: The wise men from the East
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "Simple shepherds were the first witnesses to this event." The wise men came later, guided by the star.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism gives four reasons the Word became flesh: to save us by reconciling us with God, so that we might know God's love, to be our model of holiness, and to make us partakers of the divine nature.
questions.explanation: These are the four reasons the Catechism sets out, one paragraph each. St. Peter writes that we may be made "partakers of the divine nature."

questions.prompt: The Catechism says Jesus was born in a humble stable, into a ____ family.
questions.explanation: Jesus was born in a humble stable, into a poor family, and in this poverty heaven's glory was made manifest. Luke tells us Mary laid him in a manger "because there was no room for them in the inn."

questions.prompt: According to Acts 6:8, Stephen was full of what?
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "And Stephen, full of grace and fortitude, did great wonders and signs among the people."

questions.prompt: As he died, what did Stephen ask the Lord for those who were stoning him?
choices: To send fire from heaven upon them
To let him escape from their hands
Not to lay this sin to their charge
questions.correctAnswer: Not to lay this sin to their charge
questions.explanation: Falling on his knees, Stephen cried out: "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to Acts, a young man named Saul was consenting to Stephen's death.
questions.explanation: Acts says: "And Saul was consenting to his death." This is the Saul who would become the Apostle Paul.

questions.prompt: What does the Catechism call martyrdom?
choices: The supreme witness given to the truth of the faith
A punishment for sins against the Church
A sign that God has abandoned his people
A duty laid on every Christian
questions.correctAnswer: The supreme witness given to the truth of the faith
questions.explanation: The Catechism calls martyrdom the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith: a witness borne even to death.

questions.prompt: After his parents found him in the Temple, how does Luke 2:51 describe Jesus' life at Nazareth?
choices: He studied with the doctors of the Law
He left them to begin preaching
He went to live with John in the desert
questions.explanation: Luke writes: "And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them."

questions.prompt: The Catechism says the Christian family can and should be called a ____ church.
questions.explanation: The Christian family is a specific revelation and realization of ecclesial communion, "and for this reason it can and should be called a domestic church."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Gospels tell many stories of Jesus' boyhood years at Nazareth.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says the finding of Jesus in the Temple "is the only event that breaks the silence of the Gospels about the hidden years of Jesus."

questions.prompt: According to Pope St. Paul VI, quoted in the Catechism, which three lessons does the home of Nazareth teach?
questions.explanation: Paul VI spoke of "a lesson of silence", then "A lesson on family life" and "A lesson of work."

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 2:16, why did Herod order the killing of the boys of Bethlehem?
choices: The chief priests told him the child would take his throne
He perceived that he was deluded by the wise men
The Romans ordered him to put down a rebellion
A prophet had cursed the town of Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: He perceived that he was deluded by the wise men
questions.explanation: Matthew writes: "Then Herod perceiving that he was deluded by the wise men, was exceeding angry".

questions.prompt: Which words of the prophet does Matthew see fulfilled in the mourning at Bethlehem?
choices: A star shall rise out of Jacob
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:18 reads: "A voice in Rama was heard, lamentation and great mourning; Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says the flight into Egypt and the massacre of the innocents make manifest the opposition of darkness to the light.
questions.explanation: That is the Catechism's own phrase, and it adds that Christ's whole life was lived under the sign of persecution, which his own share with him.

questions.prompt: Where did the angel tell Joseph to take the child and his mother?
questions.explanation: The angel said: "Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt". Matthew sees in the return the word "Out of Egypt have I called my son."

questions.prompt: Simeon calls the Child "A light to the revelation of the ____".
questions.explanation: Luke 2:32 reads: "A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel." The Catechism calls him the "light to the nations".

questions.prompt: What were Simeon's first words when he took the Child in his arms?
choices: My soul doth magnify the Lord, my Savior
Glory to God in the highest, and peace to men
Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord
Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away sin
questions.correctAnswer: Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord
questions.explanation: Luke 2:29 reads: "Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace".

questions.prompt: True or False: Simeon told Mary that a sword would pierce her own soul.
questions.explanation: Simeon said: "And thy own soul a sword shall pierce". The Catechism says the sword of sorrow announces Christ's perfect and unique oblation on the cross.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the presentation in the Temple show Jesus to be?
choices: A teacher of the Law, wiser than the scribes
A prophet who would call Israel back like Elijah
The firstborn Son who belongs to the Lord
A priest of the tribe of Levi, set apart for the altar
questions.correctAnswer: The firstborn Son who belongs to the Lord
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "The presentation of Jesus in the temple shows him to be the firstborn Son who belongs to the Lord."

questions.prompt: What did the prophetess Anna do when she saw the Child?
choices: She asked him to heal her of her long sickness and old age
She went at once to the palace to tell King Herod about him
She confessed to the Lord and spoke of him to all that looked for the redemption of Israel
She left the Temple for good and went home to Galilee
questions.correctAnswer: She confessed to the Lord and spoke of him to all that looked for the redemption of Israel
questions.explanation: Luke 2:38 reads: "Now she, at the same hour, coming in, confessed to the Lord; and spoke of him to all that looked for the redemption of Israel."

questions.prompt: True or False: Anna was a young woman who had only just come to the Temple.
questions.explanation: Anna was "a widow until fourscore and four years; who departed not from the temple, by fastings and prayers serving night and day."

questions.prompt: According to Luke 2:36, which tribe of Israel was Anna from?
questions.explanation: Luke calls her "the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser". Aser is the Douay-Rheims spelling of Asher.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, with Simeon and Anna what does all Israel await?
choices: The return of the prophet Elijah
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "With Simeon and Anna, all Israel awaits its encounter with the Saviour", which is the name the Byzantine tradition gives this event.

questions.prompt: Complete John 1:1: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was ____."
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."

questions.prompt: What does the Church call the fact that the Son of God assumed a human nature in order to accomplish our salvation in it?
questions.explanation: Taking up St. John's expression, the Catechism says the Church calls "Incarnation" the fact that the Son of God assumed a human nature in order to accomplish our salvation in it.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says belief in the true Incarnation of the Son of God is the distinctive sign of Christian faith.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "Belief in the true Incarnation of the Son of God is the distinctive sign of Christian faith".

questions.prompt: According to John 1:12, what does the Word give to those who receive him?
choices: Power to be made the sons of God
questions.correctAnswer: Power to be made the sons of God
questions.explanation: John writes: "But as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God, to them that believe in his name."

questions.prompt: Which council proclaimed in 431 that Mary truly became the Mother of God?
questions.explanation: In 431 the Council of Ephesus proclaimed that Mary truly became the Mother of God, because the Son of God was conceived as man in her womb.

questions.prompt: What does the title Theotokos mean?
questions.explanation: Because the One she conceived was none other than the Father's eternal Son, the Church confesses that Mary is truly "Mother of God" (Theotokos).

questions.prompt: Who called Mary "the mother of my Lord"?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth asked: "And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?"

questions.prompt: True or False: Jesus was circumcised and given his name on the eighth day after his birth.
questions.explanation: Luke writes: "And after eight days were accomplished, that the child should be circumcised, his name was called JESUS". The Catechism calls it the sign of his incorporation into Abraham's descendants.

questions.prompt: Remembering his friendship with St. Basil, St. Gregory wrote: "It seemed as if we had one soul in two ____".
questions.explanation: Benedict XVI quoted Gregory's memory of their student years: "This was our competition: not who was first but who allowed the other to be first. It seemed as if we had one soul in two bodies".

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, General Audience on St. Gregory Nazianzen, 8 August 2007

questions.prompt: From which region did Sts. Basil and Gregory come?
questions.explanation: Benedict XVI called Gregory Basil's friend and said: "like Basil, he too was a native of Cappadocia."

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, General Audience on St. Gregory Nazianzen, 8 August 2007
Benedict XVI, General Audience on St. Basil, 4 July 2007

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism teaches that the three divine Persons share the one divinity among themselves, each having a part of it.
questions.explanation: The Catechism teaches the opposite: the three Persons do not divide the one divinity among them; each of them is God whole and entire.

questions.prompt: In John 1:23, how does John the Baptist describe himself?
choices: The light of the world, come to enlighten every man
The voice of one crying out in the wilderness
The Christ of the Lord, whom Israel had awaited
A son of the prophets, sent like Elijah to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The voice of one crying out in the wilderness
questions.explanation: John said: "I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaias."

questions.prompt: What gifts did the wise men offer the Child?
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:11 reads: "they offered him gifts; gold, frankincense, and myrrh."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, in the magi the Gospel sees the first-fruits of whom?
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "In the magi, representatives of the neighbouring pagan religions, the Gospel sees the first-fruits of the nations".

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says the great feast of Epiphany celebrates the adoration of the wise men together with Jesus' baptism in the Jordan and the wedding feast at Cana.
questions.explanation: All three are named in the Catechism as manifestations of Jesus as Messiah of Israel, Son of God and Savior of the world.

questions.prompt: How did the wise men go home after they had adored the Child?
choices: With an escort of Roman soldiers, because the roads were dangerous
By ship from the port of Joppa, because the desert road was closed
Back through Jerusalem, because Herod had asked them to bring him word
Another way, because they were warned in sleep not to return to Herod
questions.correctAnswer: Another way, because they were warned in sleep not to return to Herod
questions.explanation: Matthew writes: "having received an answer in sleep that they should not return to Herod, they went back another way into their country."

questions.prompt: When he canonized her in 1975, what did Pope Paul VI say St. Elizabeth Ann Seton was the first to be?
choices: The first woman to serve in the United States Congress
The first American woman to found a university for women
The first daughter of the United States of America to be glorified as a saint
The first American woman to lead a mission to Africa
questions.correctAnswer: The first daughter of the United States of America to be glorified as a saint
questions.explanation: Paul VI said: "She is the first daughter of the United States of America to be glorified with this incomparable attribute!"

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of Elizabeth Ann Seton, 14 September 1975

questions.prompt: True or False: Pope Paul VI honored St. Elizabeth Ann Seton as a wife, a mother, a widow, and a religious.
questions.explanation: He spoke of her contribution as a woman, "a wife, a mother, a widow, and a religious." The Church teaches that all Christians in every state of life are called to holiness.

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of Elizabeth Ann Seton, 14 September 1975

questions.prompt: Where did St. Elizabeth Ann Seton establish the Sisters of Charity of Saint Joseph's?
choices: Emmitsburg, in the Archdiocese of Baltimore
Boston, in the Archdiocese of Boston
Philadelphia, in the Archdiocese of Philadelphia
New York, in the Archdiocese of New York
questions.correctAnswer: Emmitsburg, in the Archdiocese of Baltimore
questions.explanation: Paul VI said the first group, "that of the Sisters of Charity of Saint Joseph's", was "personally established by Saint Elizabeth Seton at Emmitsburg in the Archdiocese of Baltimore."

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of Elizabeth Ann Seton, 14 September 1975

questions.prompt: According to Pope Paul VI, what were St. Elizabeth Ann Seton's last words of exhortation to her sisters?
questions.explanation: Paul VI recalled the words she spoke on her deathbed on January 2, 1821: "Be children of the Church".

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of Elizabeth Ann Seton, 14 September 1975

questions.prompt: St. John Neumann was bishop of which American city?
questions.explanation: Paul VI declared a saint the Bishop of Philadelphia, in the United States of America, John Nepomucene Neumann.

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of John Neumann, 19 June 1977

questions.prompt: Through which devotion did St. John Neumann help his parishes become communities of faith and service?
questions.explanation: Paul VI said: "through the Forty Hours Devotion he helped his parishes become communities of faith and service."

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of John Neumann, 19 June 1977

questions.prompt: True or False: Pope Paul VI said St. John Neumann is the honor of all immigrants.
questions.explanation: Paul VI said: "He was close to the sick; he was at home with the poor; he was a friend to sinners. And today he is the honor of all immigrants".

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of John Neumann, 19 June 1977

questions.prompt: In Mark 6:34, why did Jesus have compassion on the multitude?
choices: Because they were sick and lame
Because they had no money to buy food
Because they were as sheep not having a shepherd
Because they had walked a long way in the heat
questions.correctAnswer: Because they were as sheep not having a shepherd
questions.explanation: Mark writes: "he had compassion on them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things."

questions.prompt: What was St. André Bessette's work at the College of Notre Dame in Montreal?
questions.explanation: Benedict XVI said: "As porter of the College of Notre Dame in Montreal, he demonstrated boundless charity and strove to relieve the distress of those who came to confide in him."

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, Homily for the canonization of André Bessette and five others, 17 October 2010

questions.prompt: What did St. André Bessette have built on Mount Royal?
questions.explanation: Benedict XVI said: "He had built the Oratory of St Joseph of Mount Royal, whose faithful custodian he remained until his death in 1937."

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, Homily for the canonization of André Bessette and five others, 17 October 2010

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says we can and should ask the saints to intercede for us and for the whole world.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "We can and should ask them to intercede for us and for the whole world."

questions.prompt: In Mark 6:50, what did Jesus say to his frightened disciples when they saw him walking on the sea?
choices: Why are you fearful, O ye of little faith?
Have a good heart, it is I, fear ye not
questions.correctAnswer: Have a good heart, it is I, fear ye not
questions.explanation: Mark writes: "And immediately he spoke with them, and said to them: Have a good heart, it is I, fear ye not."

questions.prompt: Which prophet's book was handed to Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth?
questions.explanation: Luke writes: "And the book of Isaias the prophet was delivered unto him." The Catechism says Christ made this passage of Isaiah his own to inaugurate the Good News.

questions.prompt: What does the word "Christ" mean?
questions.explanation: The Catechism says the word Christ comes from the Greek translation of the Hebrew Messiah, which means anointed. Kings, priests and, in rare instances, prophets were anointed in Israel.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says Jesus fulfilled the messianic hope of Israel in his threefold office of priest, prophet and king.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "Jesus fulfilled the messianic hope of Israel in his threefold office of priest, prophet and king."

questions.prompt: Jesus read: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me. Wherefore he hath ____ me to preach the gospel to the poor."
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18 reads: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me. Wherefore he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor".

questions.prompt: What did the man full of leprosy say to Jesus?
choices: Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean
Lord, give me money for the priests
Lord, let me follow you wherever you go
Lord, why have you not come sooner?
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean
questions.explanation: Luke 5:12 reads: "Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean."

questions.prompt: How did Jesus answer the man with leprosy?
choices: He told him his faith was too small
He touched him and said: I will. Be thou cleansed.
He sent him away to pray
He told him to wash seven times in the Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: He touched him and said: I will. Be thou cleansed.
questions.explanation: Luke 5:13 reads: "And stretching forth his hand, he touched him, saying: I will. Be thou cleansed. And immediately the leprosy departed from him."

questions.prompt: True or False: Jesus healed bodies but left the forgiving of sins to others.
questions.explanation: The Catechism teaches that Jesus has power to forgive sins as well as to heal: he came to heal the whole person, soul and body.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, Christ's compassion toward the sick is a resplendent sign of what?
choices: That sickness is a punishment for sin
That the end of the world had come
That the Temple would be rebuilt
That God has visited his people
questions.correctAnswer: That God has visited his people
questions.explanation: The Catechism says his many healings are a resplendent sign that "God has visited his people" and that the Kingdom of God is close at hand.

questions.prompt: Complete John the Baptist's words: "He must increase, but I must ____."
questions.explanation: John 3:30 reads: "He must increase, but I must decrease."

questions.prompt: In John 3:29, what does John the Baptist call himself?
questions.explanation: John says: "the friend of the bridegroom, who standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth with joy because of the bridegroom's voice."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says John the Baptist surpasses all the prophets, and is the last of them.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "John surpasses all the prophets, of whom he is the last."

questions.prompt: What did John the Baptist say when he saw Jesus coming toward him?
choices: Behold the King of the Jews
questions.explanation: John 1:29 reads: "Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world."

questions.prompt: At Jesus' baptism, in what form did the Holy Spirit descend upon him?
questions.explanation: Luke writes: "And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape, as a dove upon him".

questions.prompt: What did the voice from heaven say at Jesus' baptism, according to Mark 1:11?
choices: Glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men
Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight his paths
Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased
Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world
questions.correctAnswer: Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased
questions.explanation: Mark 1:11 reads: "And there came a voice from heaven: Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased."

questions.prompt: True or False: Jesus was baptized by John because he needed forgiveness for his own sins.
questions.explanation: Jesus had no sin. The Catechism says he allows himself to be numbered among sinners, and that our Lord voluntarily submitted himself to the baptism of St. John, intended for sinners, in order to "fulfill all righteousness."

questions.prompt: What does the Catechism call Holy Baptism?
choices: A sacrament that can be repeated each year
A sign that we have earned God's love
The basis of the whole Christian life
questions.correctAnswer: The basis of the whole Christian life
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "Holy Baptism is the basis of the whole Christian life, the gateway to life in the Spirit".

questions.prompt: In Matthew's Gospel, to whom does the angel speak in a dream about the Child conceived of the Holy Spirit?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:20 reads: "Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost." Luke tells of the angel Gabriel's message to Mary.

questions.prompt: According to Luke 2:1, why did Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem?
choices: To flee from King Herod, who sought to kill the Child
To keep the feast of the Passover in the house of David
A decree from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be enrolled
To present the Child in the Temple, as the Law required
questions.correctAnswer: A decree from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be enrolled
questions.explanation: Luke writes: "there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that the whole world should be enrolled." Joseph went to Bethlehem "because he was of the house and family of David".

questions.prompt: True or False: Only Luke's Gospel tells of the shepherds, and only Matthew's tells of the wise men.
questions.explanation: The shepherds keeping the night watches are in Luke 2; the wise men from the east are in Matthew 2.

questions.prompt: When Herod asked where the Christ should be born, which town did the chief priests and scribes name from the prophet?
questions.explanation: They said: "In Bethlehem of Juda. For so it is written by the prophet". The prophecy is Micah's: "AND THOU, BETHLEHEM Ephrata, art a little one among the thousands of Juda".

questions.prompt: The angels sang: "Glory to God in the highest; and on earth ____ to men of good will."
questions.explanation: Luke 2:14 reads: "Glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men of good will."

questions.prompt: What does the name Emmanuel mean?
questions.explanation: Matthew writes: "they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

questions.prompt: What sign did the angel give the shepherds?
choices: An infant wrapped in swaddling clothes, and laid in a manger
A voice speaking from a cloud above the town of Bethlehem
A dove coming down from heaven over a stable in the hills
A star standing over the house where the Child would be
questions.correctAnswer: An infant wrapped in swaddling clothes, and laid in a manger
questions.explanation: Luke 2:12 reads: "You shall find the infant wrapped in swaddling clothes, and laid in a manger."

questions.prompt: True or False: Matthew says Joseph wanted to expose Mary publicly.
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:19 reads: "Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing publicly to expose her, was minded to put her away privately." Then the angel told him the truth, and he took Mary as his wife.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism teaches that Jesus Christ is part God and part man.
questions.explanation: The Incarnation "does not mean that Jesus Christ is part God and part man". He became truly man while remaining truly God.

questions.prompt: Which council confessed in 451 that Christ is one person in two natures, "without confusion, change, division or separation"?
questions.explanation: The fourth ecumenical council, at Chalcedon in 451, confessed one Christ "in two natures without confusion, change, division or separation."

questions.prompt: Which heresy regarded Christ as a human person joined to the divine person of God's Son?
questions.explanation: Nestorianism made Christ a human person joined to the divine Son. St. Cyril of Alexandria and the Council of Ephesus (431) opposed it.

questions.prompt: What did the Monophysites claim about Christ?
choices: That he was only a man whom God adopted at his baptism
That he only seemed to have a body, and did not really suffer
That his human nature had ceased to exist as such when the Son assumed it
That he was the first and greatest creature God made
questions.correctAnswer: That his human nature had ceased to exist as such when the Son assumed it
questions.explanation: The Catechism says the Monophysites affirmed that the human nature had ceased to exist as such in Christ. Chalcedon answered them.

questions.prompt: The Roman liturgy sings of Christ: "What he was, he remained and what he was not, he ____".
questions.explanation: The Catechism quotes it: "What he was, he remained and what he was not, he assumed".

questions.prompt: In Philippians 2:7, what does St. Paul say Christ did, taking the form of a servant?
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "But emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men".

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says Christ worked with human hands, thought with a human mind, acted with a human will and loved with a human heart.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "The Son of God. . . worked with human hands; he thought with a human mind."

questions.prompt: According to 1 Timothy 3:16, "great is the mystery of godliness", which was manifested where?
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "great is the mystery of godliness, which was manifested in the flesh".

questions.prompt: In which town did the angel Gabriel come to Mary?
questions.explanation: Luke writes that the angel Gabriel was sent "into a city of Galilee, called Nazareth".

questions.prompt: What did Mary answer the angel?
choices: Let me first ask Joseph, to whom I am promised in marriage
Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word
I am not worthy of this honor; choose another in my place
Give me a sign, so that I may know these things are true
questions.correctAnswer: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word
questions.explanation: Luke 1:38 reads: "And Mary said: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Church has confessed from the first that Jesus was conceived solely by the power of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the Virgin Mary.
questions.explanation: From her earliest creeds the Church has confessed that Jesus was conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit alone, in the womb of the Virgin Mary.

questions.prompt: Which prophet foretold that a virgin would conceive and bear a son?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:14 reads: "Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel." The Church sees here the fulfillment of the divine promise.

questions.prompt: What does the liturgy's title for Mary, Aeiparthenos, mean?
questions.explanation: The Catechism says the liturgy of the Church celebrates Mary as Aeiparthenos, the "Ever-virgin".

questions.prompt: True or False: The Church teaches that Mary's virginity ended when she gave birth to Jesus.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says Christ's birth did not diminish his mother's virginal integrity but sanctified it, and so the Church confesses Mary's real and perpetual virginity.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does Mary's virginity manifest in the Incarnation?
choices: The power of the Roman law
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "Mary's virginity manifests God's absolute initiative in the Incarnation. Jesus has only God as Father."

questions.prompt: The angel told Mary: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall ____ thee."
questions.explanation: Luke 1:35 reads: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee."

questions.prompt: What did the wise men ask when they arrived in Jerusalem?
choices: Where is he that is born king of the Jews?
Who is the high priest this year?
Where is the house of Herod?
Where is the Temple of the Lord?
questions.correctAnswer: Where is he that is born king of the Jews?
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:2 reads: "Where is he that is born king of the Jews? For we have seen his star in the east, and are come to adore him."

questions.prompt: True or False: When Herod heard the wise men's question, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:3 reads: "And king Herod hearing this, was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him."

questions.prompt: What did Herod say he wanted to do once the wise men found the Child?
questions.explanation: Herod said: "bring me word again, that I also may come to adore him." He was lying: he sought the child to destroy him.

questions.prompt: What did the star do at the end of the wise men's journey?
choices: It stood over where the child was
It turned into an angel who greeted the Child
It disappeared, and they had to ask the way again
It fell to the earth on the hills of Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: It stood over where the child was
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:9 reads: the star "went before them, until it came and stood over where the child was."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Gospel of Matthew says there were three wise men.
questions.explanation: Matthew does not give their number. He names three gifts: "gold, frankincense, and myrrh."

questions.prompt: Which prophecy of Balaam is cited in the Catechism's footnotes on the Epiphany?
choices: A voice in Rama was heard
Out of Egypt have I called my son
A STAR SHALL RISE out of Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: A STAR SHALL RISE out of Jacob
questions.explanation: Numbers 24:17 reads: "A STAR SHALL RISE out of Jacob and a sceptre shall spring up from Israel". The Catechism speaks of the messianic light of the star of David.

questions.prompt: Isaiah 60:6 foretells: "all they from Saba shall come, bringing gold and ____".
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:6 reads: "all they from Saba shall come, bringing gold and frankincense: and shewing forth praise to the Lord."

questions.prompt: How did the wise men feel when they saw the star again?
choices: They argued about which way to go
They rejoiced with exceeding great joy
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoiced with exceeding great joy
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:10 reads: "And seeing the star they rejoiced with exceeding great joy."

questions.prompt: Besides the Vigil Mass, which three Masses does the Church celebrate on Christmas Day?
questions.explanation: The USCCB calendar lists for December 25 a Vigil Mass and three more, each with its own readings: "Night", "Dawn" and "Day".

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: In the United States, on which day is the Epiphany celebrated?
choices: The last Sunday of December, after Christmas
Always on January 6, whatever day of the week
The Sunday between January 2 and January 8
The first Monday of January, as a holiday
questions.correctAnswer: The Sunday between January 2 and January 8
questions.explanation: The USCCB calendar gives the Epiphany on the "Sunday between January 2 and January 8". In 2027 that is January 3.

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: True or False: Christmas Day and January 1, the Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God, are holy days of obligation in most of the United States.
questions.explanation: The USCCB calendar marks both as "Solemnity [Holyday of Obligation]". In Hawaii the holy days are only Christmas and the Immaculate Conception.

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: Which feast ends the Christmas season?
questions.explanation: Christmas Time ends with the Baptism of the Lord; in 2027 the next day, January 11, is a weekday in Ordinary Time. Jesus' public life begins with his baptism.

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: What liturgical color does the Church use at Christmas?
questions.explanation: The USCCB calendar gives white for the Nativity and the days of Christmas, and red for the martyrs: St. Stephen and the Holy Innocents.

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: True or False: January 1 is the Octave Day of the Nativity of the Lord.
questions.explanation: The USCCB calendar names January 1 "The Octave Day of the Nativity of the Lord" and the Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God.

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, which feasts make up the cycle surrounding the mystery of the incarnation?
choices: All Saints, All Souls, Christ the King
questions.explanation: The Catechism names "the cycle of feasts surrounding the mystery of the incarnation (Annunciation, Christmas, Epiphany)", which commemorate the beginning of our salvation.

questions.prompt: In 2026, why is the feast of St. John the Apostle not celebrated on December 27?
choices: It was removed from the calendar after Vatican II
The Sunday is given to the feast of the Holy Family
It was moved to the last week of Lent this year
It is celebrated only in Rome and in Ephesus
questions.correctAnswer: The Sunday is given to the feast of the Holy Family
questions.explanation: December 27, 2026 is a Sunday, and the USCCB calendar gives it to "THE HOLY FAMILY OF JESUS, MARY AND JOSEPH".

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: Where was Jesus baptized by John?
questions.explanation: Mark 1:9 reads: "Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan."

questions.prompt: What did John say when Jesus came to be baptized?
choices: Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
I ought to be baptized by thee, and comest thou to me?
Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand
questions.correctAnswer: I ought to be baptized by thee, and comest thou to me?
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:14 reads: "But John stayed him, saying: I ought to be baptized by thee, and comest thou to me?"

questions.prompt: Jesus answered John: "Suffer it to be so now. For so it becometh us to fulfill all ____."
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:15 reads: "For so it becometh us to fulfill all justice." The Catechism renders it "fulfil all righteousness".

questions.prompt: True or False: At Jesus' baptism the heavens were opened.
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:16 reads: "lo, the heavens were opened to him". The Catechism says these are the heavens that Adam's sin had closed.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what are the two principal effects of Baptism?
choices: Purification from sins and new birth in the Holy Spirit
Membership in a parish and a Christian name
Knowledge of Scripture and the gift of tongues
questions.correctAnswer: Purification from sins and new birth in the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "the two principal effects are purification from sins and new birth in the Holy Spirit."

questions.prompt: True or False: Baptism forgives original sin, but not personal sins.
questions.explanation: The Catechism teaches that Baptism forgives all sins, both original sin and every personal sin, and all punishment for sin.

questions.prompt: In whose name did Jesus send his apostles to baptize all nations?
choices: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the fathers of Israel
Peter and Paul, the founders of the Church in Rome
Moses and the prophets, who spoke of his coming
The Father, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: The Father, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Matthew 28:19 reads: "baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

questions.prompt: According to Romans 6:4, with whom are we buried by baptism, so that we may walk in newness of life?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:4 reads: "For we are buried together with him by baptism into death; that as Christ is risen from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also may walk in newness of life."

questions.prompt: At the wedding at Cana, what did Mary tell Jesus?
questions.explanation: John 2:3 reads: "And the wine failing, the mother of Jesus saith to him: They have no wine."

questions.prompt: Mary said to the waiters: "Whatsoever he shall say to you, ____ ye."
questions.explanation: John 2:5 reads: "His mother saith to the waiters: Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye."

questions.prompt: What did the chief steward say to the bridegroom after tasting the water made wine?
choices: Where did you buy this wine?
There is not enough for everyone
Thou hast kept the good wine until now
questions.correctAnswer: Thou hast kept the good wine until now
questions.explanation: John 2:10 reads: "Every man at first setteth forth good wine, and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse. But thou hast kept the good wine until now."

questions.prompt: True or False: John's Gospel says Jesus' first miracle was the multiplication of the loaves.
questions.explanation: John 2:11 reads: "This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee; and manifested his glory, and his disciples believed in him."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the Church see in Jesus' presence at the wedding at Cana?
choices: The calling of the first apostles to leave their homes
The confirmation of the goodness of marriage
A warning that Christians should avoid wedding feasts
The end of the Old Law and of all its purifications
questions.correctAnswer: The confirmation of the goodness of marriage
questions.explanation: The Church attaches great importance to Jesus' presence at Cana: it confirms that marriage is good, and from then on marriage will be an efficacious sign of Christ's presence.

questions.prompt: How old was Jesus when his parents took him up to Jerusalem and he stayed behind in the Temple?
questions.explanation: Luke 2:42 reads: "And when he was twelve years old, they going up into Jerusalem, according to the custom of the feast".

questions.prompt: What did Jesus say when Mary and Joseph found him in the Temple?
choices: Go home without me; I will come to Nazareth when I am ready.
I was looking for you too, but I could not find you anywhere.
I was teaching the doctors of the Law; why were you afraid?
Did you not know, that I must be about my father's business?
questions.correctAnswer: Did you not know, that I must be about my father's business?
questions.explanation: Luke 2:49 reads: "How is it that you sought me? did you not know, that I must be about my father's business?"

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says Jesus' obedience to Mary and Joseph fulfills the fourth commandment perfectly.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says: "Jesus' obedience to his mother and legal father fulfils the fourth commandment perfectly".

questions.prompt: Who is honored as the first martyr, the day after Christmas?
questions.explanation: The USCCB calendar gives December 26 to "Saint Stephen, The First Martyr". Acts tells of his stoning.

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: True or False: The Church honors the Holy Innocents, killed at Bethlehem by Herod's order, as martyrs.
questions.explanation: The USCCB calendar keeps December 28 as the feast of the Holy Innocents, Martyrs. Matthew tells of the killing in Bethlehem.

citations.reference: USCCB, Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America 2027

questions.prompt: Of which council did St. Gregory Nazianzen preside for a time, in 381?
choices: The Second Ecumenical Council, at Constantinople
The First Ecumenical Council, at Nicaea
The Third Ecumenical Council, at Ephesus
The Fourth Ecumenical Council, at Chalcedon
questions.correctAnswer: The Second Ecumenical Council, at Constantinople
questions.explanation: Benedict XVI said: "While Gregory was taking part in the Second Ecumenical Council in 381, he was elected Bishop of Constantinople and presided over the Council".

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, General Audience on St. Gregory Nazianzen, 8 August 2007

questions.prompt: St. Basil became bishop of which city in the year 370?
questions.explanation: Benedict XVI said Basil was ordained a priest "and finally, in the year 370, Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia in present-day Turkey."

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, General Audience on St. Basil, 4 July 2007

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton was born and raised in New York in the Episcopalian Communion before she became Catholic.
questions.explanation: Paul VI said: "Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton was born, brought up and educated in New York in the Episcopalian Communion."

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of Elizabeth Ann Seton, 14 September 1975

questions.prompt: What did St. John Neumann promote, according to Pope Paul VI, "with relentless energy"?
choices: A Catholic daily newspaper for the whole country
The Catholic school system in the United States
Missions to the native peoples of the West
A new English translation of the whole Bible
questions.correctAnswer: The Catholic school system in the United States
questions.explanation: Paul VI said he helped children "by promoting, with relentless energy, the Catholic school system in the United States."

citations.reference: Paul VI, Homily for the canonization of John Neumann, 19 June 1977

questions.prompt: In which year did St. André Bessette die?
questions.explanation: Benedict XVI said he remained the faithful custodian of the Oratory of St Joseph of Mount Royal "until his death in 1937."

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, Homily for the canonization of André Bessette and five others, 17 October 2010

questions.prompt: Which religious congregation did St. André Bessette belong to?
choices: The Society of Jesus, the Jesuits
The Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer
The Order of Friars Minor, the Franciscans
The Congregation of the Holy Cross
questions.correctAnswer: The Congregation of the Holy Cross
questions.explanation: Benedict XVI called him "a native of Quebec in Canada, and a religious of the Congregation of the Holy Cross".

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, Homily for the canonization of André Bessette and five others, 17 October 2010
